front: Which three tenses do you need to talk about holidays in Spanish?
answer: preterite / present / conditional
title: Holidays and Travel Plans

front: What are the six preterite forms of 'ir' (to go)?
answer: fui / fuiste / fue / fuimos / fuisteis / fueron
title: Holidays and Travel Plans

front: Why can 'fui' mean either 'I went' or 'I was'?
answer: Because ir and ser share identical preterite forms, so context tells you which meaning is intended.
title: Holidays and Travel Plans

front: Why do verbs like tener and salir take irregular stems in the conditional tense?
answer: They use irregular stems that are the same as the stems used in the future tense.
title: Holidays and Travel Plans

front: In 'El hotel era bonito y tenía piscina', why is the imperfect used instead of the preterite?
answer: Because the imperfect describes what the hotel was like, while the preterite is used for the action of staying there.
title: Accommodation and Hotels

front: Why is 'quisiera' used instead of 'quiero' when booking a hotel room?
answer: Quisiera is more polite and formal than quiero, showing you can vary your register when making requests.
title: Accommodation and Hotels

front: What five comparative structures does the lesson give for comparing types of transport?
answer: más … que / menos … que / tan … como / mejor … que / peor … que
title: Transport and Directions

front: What three connectives can you use to give a reason for a transport choice?
answer: porque es / dado que es / ya que es
title: Transport and Directions

front: How do you say you travel by a particular type of transport in Spanish?
answer: You use en plus the vehicle, such as en coche or en tren, except for a pie and a caballo, which don't take en.
title: Transport and Directions

front: How do you form a comparison of equality, such as 'as comfortable as', in Spanish?
answer: You use tan followed by the adjective and then como, as in tan cómodo como (as comfortable as).
title: Transport and Directions

front: Which five verb forms does the lesson use across different weather expressions?
answer: hace / llueve / nieva / hay / está
title: Weather and Holiday Activities

front: What are the six forms of 'estar' (imperfect) used to build the past continuous?
answer: yo estaba / tú estabas / él/ella estaba / nosotros estábamos / vosotros estabais / ellos estaban
title: Weather and Holiday Activities

front: Why does 'nadar' form its gerund as 'nadando' but 'comer' forms it as 'comiendo'?
answer: Because -ar verbs add -ando to make the gerund, while -er and -ir verbs add -iendo instead.
title: Weather and Holiday Activities

front: Why might a holiday description combine the preterite (fui) with the imperfect (hacía)?
answer: The preterite shows the completed action of going on holiday, while the imperfect describes the ongoing weather in the background.
title: Weather and Holiday Activities

front: Which four tenses should a strong answer about technology use, to show range?
answer: present / preterite / imperfect / future
title: Technology and Social Media

front: What three advantages of technology does the lesson give?
answer: you can keep in touch with friends abroad / you can search for information quickly / it can be fast
items: you can keep in touch with friends abroad
you can search for information quickly
title: Technology and Social Media

front: How do you form the past participle of a regular -ar verb like comprar, for the perfect tense?
answer: You remove -ar and add -ado, so comprar becomes comprado (bought).
title: Technology and Social Media

front: Why might you use 'por un lado… por otro lado…' when discussing technology?
answer: It structures a balanced argument by contrasting one side of an issue with the other.
title: Technology and Social Media

front: Which three time-frames does a strong description of your home cover?
answer: present / imperfect / conditional
title: My House and Home

front: What is the difference between using 'hay' and using 'tiene' when describing your home?
answer: Hay says what there is in a room, while tiene says what your house itself has, like its number of bedrooms.
title: My House and Home

front: How does 'hay' work differently from English 'there is' and 'there are'?
answer: Hay is the same word for both singular and plural, unlike English, which distinguishes 'there is' from 'there are'.
title: My House and Home

front: Which three time-frames does a strong answer about your town cover?
answer: present (hay) / imperfect (había) / conditional (habría / tendría)
title: My Town and Local Area

front: How do you make 'se puede' negative, to say something isn't possible?
answer: You put no in front of it, as in no se puede hacer mucho por la noche (you can't do much at night).
title: My Town and Local Area

front: How does 'La ciudad es más ruidosa pero tiene más tiendas' compare the city to the village?
answer: It uses pero to contrast two qualities — the city is noisier, but it has more shops.
title: My Town and Local Area

front: Which three tenses does a strong answer about environmental issues use?
answer: present / preterite / future or conditional
title: The Environment and Global Issues

front: What four structures can you use to say what should or must be done, each followed by an infinitive?
answer: Se debe / Deberíamos / Hay que / Es importante
title: The Environment and Global Issues

front: Why do verbs like tener and hacer use irregular stems in the future tense?
answer: They have irregular stems, which are the same stems used in the conditional tense (tener → tendré, hacer → haré).
title: The Environment and Global Issues

front: What's the difference in meaning between 'se debe' and 'deberíamos' when talking about obligations?
answer: Se debe means 'one must' and is impersonal, while deberíamos means 'we should', including yourself and others.
title: The Environment and Global Issues

front: What are the four forms of a Spanish adjective ending in -o, like 'alto'?
answer: alto / alta / altos / altas
title: Family and Describing People

front: What six connectives does the lesson give for linking descriptions?
answer: y / pero / también / sin embargo / además / aunque
title: Family and Describing People

front: Why is 'trabajadora' irregular as the feminine form of 'trabajador'?
answer: Trabajador doesn't end in -o, so instead of changing a letter, it simply adds -a to make trabajadora.
title: Family and Describing People

front: Why don't 'mayor' and 'menor' change when describing family members of different genders?
answer: Because mayor and menor stay the same for both masculine and feminine nouns; they never change for gender.
title: Family and Describing People

front: Why does 'llevarse bien/mal con' change form depending on who is speaking?
answer: Because it's a reflexive verb, so its pronoun, such as me or se, changes to match the subject.
title: Friendships and Relationships

front: Why do phrases like 'a mi modo de ver' count as more sophisticated than 'me gusta'?
answer: They go beyond the basic me gusta and no me gusta, showing a wider range of opinion language.
title: Friendships and Relationships

front: What are the six conditional forms of 'hablar' (to speak), one for each subject pronoun?
answer: hablaría / hablarías / hablaría / hablaríamos / hablaríais / hablarían
title: Relationships and Marriage

front: Why do verbs like tener and poder change their stems in the conditional (tendría, podría)?
answer: They drop the -e- or -i- from the infinitive, and some add a -d-, before the regular endings are attached.
title: Relationships and Marriage

front: How do 'ser' and 'ir' form their conditional stems differently from verbs like 'tener'?
answer: Ser and ir simply keep their infinitive as the stem, unlike tener, which drops letters and adds -d-.
title: Relationships and Marriage

front: What three structures does the lesson give for expressing obligation in Spanish?
answer: Se debe + infinitive / Deber + infinitive / Tener que + infinitive
title: Healthy Living and Lifestyle

front: What five healthy habits does the lesson list under 'hábitos saludables'?
answer: eat a balanced diet / drink lots of water / exercise regularly / sleep eight hours every night / eat fruits and vegetables
title: Healthy Living and Lifestyle

front: Why is 'Debo como' wrong, when 'Debo comer' is correct?
answer: After a modal verb like debo, the second verb must stay in the infinitive, not be conjugated again.
title: Healthy Living and Lifestyle

front: Why does 'equilibrada' end in -a in the phrase 'una dieta equilibrada'?
answer: Because dieta is a feminine noun, so the adjective equilibrada takes the feminine -a ending to agree with it.
title: Healthy Living and Lifestyle

front: What three main meals does the lesson give for the Spanish day?
answer: el desayuno (breakfast) / la comida / el almuerzo (lunch) / la cena (dinner/supper)
title: Food, Drink and Mealtimes

front: What four Spanish verbs does the lesson give for having breakfast, lunch, dinner and an afternoon snack?
answer: desayunar / almorzar / comer / cenar / merendar
title: Food, Drink and Mealtimes

front: Why might a description of food and mealtimes use present, preterite and conditional tenses together?
answer: It shows what you usually eat, what you ate in the past, and what you'd like to try, covering a range of tenses.
title: Food, Drink and Mealtimes

front: How does 'quisiera' differ from 'me gustaría' when asking for something politely?
answer: Quisiera comes from querer and is even more formal and polite than me gustaría, though both mean 'I would like'.
title: Food, Drink and Mealtimes

front: What are the six indirect object pronouns used with 'doler' (to hurt)?
answer: me / te / le / nos / os / les
title: Body Parts, Illness and Ailments

front: Why does 'doler' become 'duele' in one sentence and 'duelen' in another?
answer: Duele is used for a singular body part and duelen for a plural body part, since doler works like gustar.
title: Body Parts, Illness and Ailments

front: Why does 'tengo frío' literally translate as 'I have cold' rather than 'I am cold'?
answer: Spanish uses tener (to have) for conditions like being cold or hungry, where English uses the verb 'to be'.
title: Body Parts, Illness and Ailments

front: What six structures does the lesson give for giving impersonal advice, each followed by an infinitive?
answer: Se debe / Hay que / Es importante / Es necesario / Es aconsejable / Es imprescindible
title: Drugs, Smoking and Alcohol

front: What five reasons does the lesson give for why people smoke?
answer: it makes you feel more grown-up / it relaxes me / it gives me confidence / everyone in my class smokes / they make fun of me if I don't
items: it makes you feel more grown-up
they make fun of me if I don't
title: Drugs, Smoking and Alcohol

front: How do you turn 'se debe' into a negative meaning 'one must not'?
answer: You add no in front of it, as in no se debe fumar (one must not smoke).
title: Drugs, Smoking and Alcohol

front: What four adjective endings mark singular masculine, singular feminine, plural masculine and plural feminine subjects?
answer: -o / -a / -os / -as
title: School Subjects and Opinions
problems: names a board or the exam

front: What six positive opinion phrases does the lesson give for describing school subjects?
answer: me gusta(n) / me encanta(n) / me chifla(n) / me apasiona(n) / me entretiene(n) / mi asignatura preferida es
title: School Subjects and Opinions

front: Why does 'me gusta' change to 'me gustan' when talking about 'las matemáticas'?
answer: The verb ending matches the subject that is liked, not the person; matemáticas is plural, so gusta becomes gustan.
title: School Subjects and Opinions

front: Why does 'porque es' change to 'porque son' when giving a reason about school subjects?
answer: Porque es is used for a singular subject and porque son for a plural subject, matching the noun being described.
title: School Subjects and Opinions

front: What six key phrases does the lesson give for describing your school day?
answer: classes start at half past eight / classes finish at three / we have break at half past ten / in the morning / in the afternoon / we have a lot of homework
items: classes start at half past eight
we have break at half past ten
we have a lot of homework
title: Teachers, School Day and Facilities

front: What four Spanish time expressions mean five, ten, twenty and twenty-five minutes past the hour?
answer: y cinco / y diez / y veinte / y veinticinco
title: Teachers, School Day and Facilities

front: Why is 'es la una' singular while 'son las dos/tres' and so on are plural?
answer: Es la una is used only for one o'clock; son las is used for every other hour, which is plural.
title: Teachers, School Day and Facilities

front: Why is 'hay' the same word whether you mean 'there is' or 'there are'?
answer: Hay doesn't change for singular or plural; it's used the same way, as in hay una biblioteca or hay muchos laboratorios.
title: Teachers, School Day and Facilities

front: What are the six forms of 'ir a' used for the near future tense, one per subject pronoun?
answer: voy a / vas a / va a / vamos a / vais a / van a
title: School Rules, Homework and Future Plans

front: What six structures does the lesson give for expressing obligation and prohibition?
answer: Se debe / No se debe / Se puede / No se puede / Tengo que / Debo
title: School Rules, Homework and Future Plans

front: Why is 'homework' always plural in Spanish ('los deberes'), even though English treats it as singular?
answer: Deberes is a word that's always used in the plural in Spanish, unlike the English word 'homework', which is singular.
title: School Rules, Homework and Future Plans

front: Why don't verbs like tener and hacer simply add future endings to their normal infinitive?
answer: They use irregular stems instead, such as tendr- for tener and har- for hacer, before the regular future endings.
title: School Rules, Homework and Future Plans

front: What are the six present-tense forms of 'jugar' (to play), one per subject pronoun?
answer: juego / juegas / juega / jugamos / jugáis / juegan
title: Free-Time Activities and Hobbies

front: Why might you use 'lo que más me gusta es' instead of always writing 'me gusta'?
answer: It varies your language beyond the basic me gusta, showing you can express opinions in more than one way.
title: Free-Time Activities and Hobbies

front: What six negative adjectives or phrases does the lesson give for something you dislike watching?
answer: aburrido/a / tonto/a / lento/a / repetitivo/a / horroroso/a / una pérdida de tiempo
title: Music, Film and Television

front: What six-point scale, from most positive to most negative, does the lesson give for opinions on entertainment?
answer: me encanta / me fascina / me chifla / me gusta mucho / me mola / me gusta bastante / no me gusta / no me interesa / me aburre / me molesta / no soporto / odio / detesto
items: me encanta / me fascina / me chifla
no me gusta / no me interesa
me aburre / me molesta / no soporto
title: Music, Film and Television

front: Why does 'me encanta' change to 'me encantan' in 'me encantan las películas de acción'?
answer: Encantan agrees with películas, the thing being liked, which is plural and acts as the subject of the sentence.
title: Music, Film and Television

front: Why does 'divertido' become 'divertida' when describing a feminine singular noun?
answer: Adjectives must agree with the noun; a feminine singular noun takes the -a ending instead of the masculine -o.
title: Music, Film and Television

front: Which three tenses does the lesson use to talk about sport?
answer: present / preterite / future
title: Sport and Exercise

front: What six team sports does the lesson list?
answer: fútbol / baloncesto / voleibol / rugby / hockey / cricket
title: Sport and Exercise

front: Why does Spanish use 'jugar a' for football but 'hacer' for swimming?
answer: Jugar a is used for team or ball sports, while hacer is used for individual activities like swimming.
title: Sport and Exercise

front: Why is only the 'yo' form of 'hacer' irregular in the present tense?
answer: Hacer changes to hago just for I; the other forms, haces, hace, hacemos and hacen, follow the regular pattern.
title: Sport and Exercise

front: What three polite phrases does the lesson give for ordering in a restaurant?
answer: Para mí… / Quisiera… / Me gustaría…
title: Eating Out and Restaurant Conversations

front: What six useful phrases does the lesson give for a restaurant conversation?
answer: do you have a table for two / I would like to book a table / what do you recommend / what is the dish of the day / the bill, please / is service included
items: do you have a table for two
I would like to book a table
what is the dish of the day
title: Eating Out and Restaurant Conversations

front: Why is it best to avoid saying just 'quiero' when ordering food?
answer: Quiero on its own is informal and can sound rude; quisiera or me gustaría are more polite alternatives.
title: Eating Out and Restaurant Conversations

front: What four festivals does this lesson cover?
answer: Las Fallas / La Tomatina / Semana Santa / El Día de los Muertos
title: Spanish Festivals and Celebrations

front: What five key vocabulary items does the lesson give for La Tomatina?
answer: tirar tomates / divertirse / llevar ropa vieja / participar / una batalla
title: Spanish Festivals and Celebrations

front: What four meals structure the daily schedule in Spain, in order?
answer: el desayuno / la comida / la merienda / la cena
title: Customs and Traditions

front: What three areas does the lesson compare between Spain and the UK?
answer: mealtimes / school hours / social life
title: Customs and Traditions

front: How do you introduce a contrast when comparing Spain to England, using 'a diferencia de'?
answer: You start with a diferencia de Inglaterra (unlike England), then describe how Spain differs.
title: Customs and Traditions

front: What five imperfect-tense verbs does the lesson give for describing what someone used to be, have or do?
answer: era / tenía / llevaba / hacía / iba
title: Celebrity Culture and Role Models

front: What six things does the lesson list as signs of positive celebrity influence?
answer: has good values / helps the poor / donates money to good causes / volunteers at soup kitchens / raises money for charity / talks about mental health issues
title: Celebrity Culture and Role Models

front: How do you justify that someone is a good role model in Spanish?
answer: Use porque followed by a personality adjective and evidence, as in 'es generosa y dona dinero a buenas causas'.
title: Celebrity Culture and Role Models

front: What five advantages of social media does the lesson give?
answer: a good way to stay in touch / you can share photos and experiences / useful for studying / lets you meet people from other countries / entertaining and fun
items: a good way to stay in touch
you can share photos and experiences
lets you meet people from other countries
title: Social Media and Online Life

front: What six disadvantages of social media does the lesson give?
answer: can be addictive / cyberbullying is a serious problem / you waste a lot of time / can affect mental health / there are privacy risks / people share an unrealistic image of their life
items: you waste a lot of time
people share an unrealistic image of their life
title: Social Media and Online Life

front: Why is 'aunque' a useful word when discussing both advantages and disadvantages of social media?
answer: Aunque means 'although' and lets you show contrast, linking a positive point with a negative one in one sentence.
title: Social Media and Online Life
